caseStudies.subtitle: Some builds, told the way I think about them — problem, approach, result.

items.problem: The Brazilian coupon market is full of slow, stale-data sites — there was no platform with real affiliate sync, smart search and alerts that fire before deals expire.
items.approach: Built a full-stack system with 5 affiliate sources via Adapter Pattern, BullMQ queues syncing every 3h, Meilisearch full-text search, double opt-in alerts and algorithmic scoring 0–100 by discount and expiry.
items.result: A live platform with automatic sync of thousands of coupons, O(1) DB roundtrips for alert matching, 3-level threaded comments and a complete admin panel for coupons, stores and users.

items.problem: A real-time crash game only earns player trust if every round can be verified — it's not enough to promise the outcome is fair.
items.approach: Implemented a provably fair algorithm with a cryptographic hash per round and synced all clients via WebSocket, keeping the multiplier identical in real time for everyone.
items.result: Every result is reproducible and auditable by the player, with the multiplier curve streamed live, with no divergence between sessions.

items.problem: Dropshipping stores in Brazil hit a wall at checkout: international gateways break conversion and catalog management with local suppliers is usually manual.
items.approach: Built the store in Next.js with national checkout via Stripe and direct integration with BR suppliers, automating catalog sync and the order flow.
items.result: An end-to-end e-commerce with national payment and an integrated catalog — less manual work and a checkout designed for the Brazilian customer.
